steps.decide: What the badge is telling the reader: status, count or category
Whether the text is read in place or hidden from the reading order
How counts cap, pluralise and localise
When a badge should have been plain text

rules.statement: A badge does exactly one of three jobs — status, count or category — and its shape differs per job so a count is never mistaken for a state.
A status badge is in the reading order once, attached to its object; a decorative dot has no text, and a count badge on a navigation item is folded into the link's accessible name.
Counts cap at 99+ with the exact number still available in the accessible name, are pluralised with the locale's rules, and are formatted with the locale's digits.
Status colour is always paired with text or an icon whose shape differs, because a red dot and a green dot are the same dot to a colour-blind reader.
If the value is a sentence the reader needs, it is text; a page where every row carries a coloured badge has no status signal at all.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a count that updates from a live feed applies only if it is newer than the rendered value; a lower stale value never overwrites a higher fresh one

motion.motion: a static muted badge holds the layout over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the muted badge appears with no animation

motion.motion: the badge cross-fades to its value over 140ms
motion.reducedMotion: the value appears instantly and is announced once

motion.motion: a neutral 'unknown' badge replaces the placeholder over 120ms
the badge returns to its muted placeholder over 120ms
the count nudges 1 px up and settles over 160ms
motion.reducedMotion: the count changes instantly with no movement

motion.motion: the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: State one fact about an object in a way that is scannable and still says the same thing to someone who cannot see the colour.
useCases: see that an invoice is overdue
see three unread items in a list
see that a record is archived
nicheDifferences: Badges are the most over-used element in admin products: they are cheap to add and quickly become noise
The discipline is that a badge must change a decision or it is decoration
inputs: whether the fact is a state, a count or a category
the vocabulary of states and whether each has a colour
anatomy: an optional icon whose shape differs per state
a count badge with a cap
an accessible name that includes the fact
styling: status pills use a tinted background at 12% with full-strength text
count badges are a filled circle at least 16 px with 1 px optical alignment
never two badge styles in one row
a11y: status is text first; colour is secondary and not the only signal
a count badge inside a link is part of that link's accessible name
'unknown' is a real state, not an empty badge
responsive: count badges keep their cap readable at 320 px
status pills wrap below the label rather than truncating it
long category names truncate in the middle with the full value available
copy: states are named from the object's vocabulary: 'Overdue', not 'Status 3'
counts read '99+' with 'more than 99' in the accessible name
'unknown' rather than an empty or zero badge
alternatives: plain text in a table cell when the value is read row by row
a chip when the value filters
an icon plus text when the state is binary
acceptance: each badge does one job and its shape matches the job
status is paired with text and never carried by colour alone
counts cap at 99+ with the exact number in the accessible name
an unknown state exists rather than an empty badge
a count badge inside a link is part of that link's name
failureCases: red and green dots are the only difference between paid and overdue
a count badge is announced twice, once by the badge and once by the link
counts render as '1000' and break the layout
every row carries a badge so none of them means anything

refused.reason: a status label is not pressable; a pressable status is a filter chip
a status describes an object and is never inert
a count is informational; if it cannot be shown it is omitted
a category label is not a button unless it filters, in which case it is a chip
